I’m a 49-year-old man who’s worked these plots in Quzhou since I was a teenager. My father farmed them before me, and he taught me the wheat-maize rotation that most families around here rely on. I only went to primary school, so I don’t mess around with fancy new methods I don’t fully understand; I stick to what the land and the weather have proven to work year after year. I have about 8 mu in total, and last October I put winter wheat on every bit of it because the soil on the North China Plain is suited to wheat and there’s always a buyer for both grain and corn. Now that spring has arrived, the wheat is greening up. I’ll irrigate three more times—at jointing, heading, and grain filling—and top-dress nitrogen and spray when I see aphids or rust. After harvest in early June, the window is short, so I’ll rotary-till the stubble and plant hybrid maize seed immediately. I’ll irrigate the maize twice if the summer rains are light, and fertilize according to the shop’s usual recommendation. This double crop gives me two harvests and keeps cash coming in for the household.
